brief.problem_or_goal: To discuss the development and potential of a new, local, cross-platform TTS engine.
brief.context: A community member is sharing information about a newly released local TTS engine called KokoroSharp, written in C#, which is available as a NuGet package and has open-source code.
brief.motivation: This question is worth discussing to understand the capabilities and potential applications of local TTS solutions for LLM enthusiasts who might be interested in offline AI voice chat or other speech synthesis projects.
brief.desired_response: A discussion about the technical aspects, potential use cases, and community reception of the KokoroSharp TTS engine.
brief.speaker_relationship_to_source: reader of archived source; no claim of personally running reported tests

facts.text: The author was working on a fully offline AI voice chat app that was about 90% ready to release.
facts.evidence_quote: So, to start with, I am working on a fully offline AI voice chat app, and while it's about 90% ready to release, a specific new, high-performance audio model came out
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: A new, high-performance audio model, referred to as "Kokoro," prompted the author to build a local, cross-platform TTS engine.
facts.evidence_quote:
a specific new, high-performance audio model came out (\*stares at Kokoro\*).

What did I do?

I dropped everything to build a local, cross-platform TTS engine!
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The developed TTS engine is described as "Beginner-friendly yet flexible."
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The KokoroSharp TTS engine is available on NuGet.
facts.evidence_quote: It's available on [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/KokoroSharp/)! Just install the package and you're ready!
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The source code for KokoroSharp is open and available on GitHub.
facts.evidence_quote: And, of course, the source is open: [https://github.com/Lyrcaxis/KokoroSharp](https://github.com/Lyrcaxis/KokoroSharp)
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The example code demonstrates loading a KokoroTTS model and getting a voice named "af_heart" using KokoroVoiceManager.
facts.evidence_quote:
KokoroTTS tts = KokoroTTS.LoadModel();
    KokoroVoice heartVoice = KokoroVoiceManager.GetVoice("af_heart");
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement
